data_status: STRICT MODE: this dataset contains only values that were compared with, or ingested directly from, retrieved sources: JPL (SSD, SBDB, NHATS), NASA (NSSDC fact sheets and mission catalog, Small Spacecraft SoA report 2026, SLS page, Apollo 11 press kit, NTRS papers, data.nasa.gov), ULA, ESA, NIST, and the Launch Library 2 aggregator. Records carry source_authority/confidence where the source is an aggregator or vendor-reported compilation. Recalled, estimated and fictional values (optimizer catalog, costs, engine/vehicle specs without a retrievable source, the user-supplied SpaceX table) are not included. Derived values are computed only from verified inputs and are labelled derived.

record.name: Infrared Radiometers
record.description: This experiment, carried on both Pioneers 10 and 11, was designed to measure the irradiance of Jupiter's atmosphere and surface in two ranges of thermal (IR) wavelengths -- 14 to 25 and 19 to 56 micrometers. These measurements provided data on the net thermal energy flux of Jupiter and its deviation from a blackbody spectrum. In addition, detailed information was provided on the atmospheric thermal structure and chemical composition of the planet. The instrumentation for this experiment was similar to that carried on the Mariners 6 and 7 flights in 1969 but had higher resolution. It was a two-channel IR radiometer employing a pair of 88-channel, thin-film bimetallic thermocouples, illuminated through appropriate optics by a 7.62-cm reflecting Cassegrain telescope with a 1-deg by 0.3-deg field of view. Analysis of the data was to help resolve: (1) whether Jupiter is radiating a significant amount of internal energy, (2) the existence of a frozen methane polar cap, (3) the brightness temperature on the dark hemisphere, and (4) the existence of thermal discontinuities in the atmosphere. This instrument was turned off in January 1974 after a failure of unknown origin.
